title: Ctrl-Adapter source-control x target-backbone bridge views
hypothesis: A learned source-encoder x target-backbone-decoder bridge predicts heldout control/backbone pairs with <=0.02 relative error at >=25% fewer complete bytes and MACs than independent pair bridges.
physical_object: source-control to target-backbone linear feature bridges
mirror_coordinate: source control ID and target backbone ID selecting shared encoder and decoder factors

development.selection_metric: heldout pair operator nRMSE; actual serialized bytes; active MAC proxy

fresh.reason: single scoped mechanism screen; no audit opened after development and native alias assessment

paid_objects: full bridge matrices for independent control

success_gate: Heldout nRMSE <=0.02, >=25% fewer complete bytes and MACs than independent bridges, and a strict quality-byte-compute improvement over the native two-tower control.
failure_gate: Quality/byte/compute gate miss or exact native two-tower payload/function alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific value.
boundaries: Synthetic linear bridges only; no pretrained ControlNet, image/video diffusion backbone or image-generation quality.
Teacher pair bridges are generated by a shared two-tower factorization; this is an aligned mechanism screen.
No accelerator runtime or near-convergence capacity claim.
